FF161 adds support for NavigationTransition.to in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1991959

This improves the docs for the feature:

  • NavigationTransition.to: says what the property is for, adds a Description section, and replaces the example (which used an undefined variable) with one that reports which navigation failed.
  • NavigationDestination: mentions that it's also returned by NavigationTransition.to, and id/index/key describe the traverse condition without tying it to NavigateEvent.navigationType.

Related docs work can be tracked in #46461

FF161 enables support for Clipboard API web custom formats (MIME types prefixed with web ) by default in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2053725

Summary below, but mostly this is better cross-linking.

This fixes some gaps in the custom formats docs:

  • ClipboardItem(), ClipboardItem, ClipboardItem.types, ClipboardItem.getType() and ClipboardItem.supports() now mention and link to custom formats.
  • Clipboard.write(): NotAllowedError also covers unsupported types, including a web type that isn't a correctly structured MIME type.
  • Clipboard API overview: security note that custom format data may have been written by another site or application.
  • Minor: a typo, and reload(true) → reload() in the examples.

Related docs work can be tracked in #46463
items.title: FF161 Clipboard API web custom formats: docs fixes

Description

This PR adds the page for emulation.setGeolocationOverride command, with corresponding updates to the module overview page and the sidebar.

Note

The Firefox note in BCD explicitly states that the global configuration is not yet supported.
My testing in Chrome shows the same limitation: omitting both scope selectors returns invalid argument: “Either user contexts or browsing contexts must be provided”. However, there's no such note for Chrome in BCD.

The current version of the page aligns with the spec to say that session-wide overrides are applied when neither contexts nor userContexts is specified. Let me know if this needs to be changed to the implemented behaviour instead.

Spec link

  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-emulation-setGeolocationOverride

Project tracker: mdn/mdn#851

Extensions can only get the window of a sender through sender.tab.windowId, which needs a tab. windowId is also set for senders such as popups and sidebars. Firefox 160 supports it and Safari is adding it.

items.content_html:
Description

Corrects the code parameter docs for WebSocket.close(). When close() is called without a code, the close frame is sent with no status code, so the server sees 1005 ("No Status Received"), not 1000. The page now also explains that the code of the browser's close event is taken from the server's reply.

Motivation

The page currently says an omitted code is set to 1000 for a normal closure. No code is sent at all. Readers who rely on the current text (for example, checking for 1000 on the server) get unexpected results. The browser-side code also depends on how the server replies, which the page didn't mention.

I verified this in Chrome and Firefox, and with Node's built-in WebSocket, against a raw server that logs the exact close frame it receives:

  • In all cases, the client's close frame had an empty payload (no status code).
  • The close event code mirrors the server's reply: 1005 when the server echoes the empty frame, 1000 when the server replies with 1000, and 1006 (wasClean: false) when the server drops the connection without replying.

Additional details

  • WHATWG WebSockets spec, close(): if neither code nor reason is present, "the WebSocket Close message must not have a body".
  • RFC 6455 §7.1.5: the connection close code is the status code in the first close frame received. If that frame contains no status code, the close code is considered to be 1005.
  • RFC 6455 §5.5.1: an endpoint replying to a close frame typically echoes the status code it received.

Related issues and pull requests

None.
items.title: Fix default close code for WebSocket.close() with no arguments

items.content_html:
Description

The radial-gradient() CSS function allows explicitly defining the radial-size and position values of the gradient, but there are no ready-to-go examples on the current version of the MDN page. This PR adds a couple examples to the page.

Motivation

At the moment it is difficult to understand from the page that defining those properties of a gradient is possible. It would be helpful to have examples that people can easily understand and use.

Additional details

For convenience, here are the examples I'd like to add:

/* Try it */
background: radial-gradient(ellipse 75% 50% at 15% 85%, #ffff00, transparent); 
/* Syntax */
/* A gradient with a specific ellipse size and center */
radial-gradient(ellipse 100% 25% at 0% 50%, red, blue)
items.title: Add a radial-size and position example to `radial-gradient()`
